רָפָא verb heal (Late Hebrew in derivatives; Phoenician רפא, Syriac heal; on Aramaic proper name compounded with רפא see NöZMG xi (1886), 723 Lzb369; Sabean proper name אלרפא Langer1, 1 DHMZMG xxxvii (1883), 326; Arabic (and ) darn, mend, repair, pacify; Ethiopic stitch together, mend; compare KüchenmeisterZWiss. Th. xxx (1887), 257 ff.); —

Qal Perfect 3 masculine singular consecutive ׳וְר Isa 6:10, suffix וּרְפָאָם Isa 19:22, 1 singular suffix consecutive וּרְפָאתִיו Isa 57:19, etc.; Imperfect 3 masculine singular יִרְפָּא 2Kgs 20:8 +, suffix יִרְפָּאֵנוּ Hos 6:1, 1 singular אֶרְפָּא Hos 14:5 +, אֶרְפָּה (Ges«GKC:75pp»§ 75pp) Jer 3:22 3 feminine plural תִּרְפֶּינָה (Idib. qq) Job 5:18, etc.; Imperative masculine singular רְפָא Num 12:13, רְפָה (Idib. pp) Ps 60:4, רְפָאָ֫ה Ps 41:5, etc.; Infinitive absolute רָפוֺא Isa 19:22 construct לִרְפֹּא Hos 5:13, etc.; Participle רֹפֵא 2Kgs 20:5 +, etc.; — heal:
1. literally,
\ \ a. of God, with accusative of person Gen 20:17 (E), Ps 107:20 (suffix), with ל person Num 12:13 (JE) 2Kgs 20:5; 2Kgs 20:8.
\ \ b. of men, absolute Eccl 3:3 (opposed to הרג); participle as substantive healer, physician, Gen 50:2 (twice in verse) (J) 2Chr 16:12.
2. figurative, heal hurts of nation, involving ׳י's (restored) favour (and, often, forgiveness):
\ \ a. subject ׳י, with suffix person, Hos 6:1; Hos 11:3 (yet compare We Now), Exod 15:26 (J), Isa 19:22b Isa 57:18; Isa 57:19; Jer 33:6; Ps 30:3, compare Ps 6:3 with accusative עַם 2Chr 30:20, with accusative אֶרֶץ 2Chr 7:14 with ל of nation Hos 7:1, and (indefinite subject) Isa 6:10 (lest) one heal them (= passive, they be healed); with accusative of hurt, מִחַץ מַכָּתוֺ Isa 30:26, שְׁבָרִים (of land) Ps 60:4, so מְשׁוּבָה Hos 14:5; Jer 3:22 (including the consequences of backsliding); with ל of hurt Ps 103:3 accusative nation (personified) + מִן of hurt Jer 30:17 I will heal thee of thy wounds (|| אֶרְפָּאֵךְ); absolute Isa 19:22a (opposed to נגף), Deut 32:39 (opposed to מחץ); participle as substantive healer, physician Jer 8:22.
\ \ b. human subject, with ל of nation, Hos 5:13, compare Lam 2:13.
3. a. figurative, heal individual distresses, with suffix person Jer 17:14, with accusative נַפְשִׁי = me Jer 41:5, with ל person, לִשְׁבוּרֵי לֵב Ps 147:3 (i.e. longing exiles, compare Isa 61:3); absolute Job 5:18 (opposed to מחץ); participle as substantive Job 13:4. Niph`al Perfect 3 masculine singular נִרְפָּא Lev 13:37 +, 3 feminine singular נִרְפָּ֑תָה (Ges«GKC:75qq»§ 75qq) Jer 51:9 3 plural וְנִרְפּאו consecutive Ezek 47:8 Imperfect 2 masculine singular תֵּרָפֵא Jer 51:8 3 masculine plural יֵרָֽפְאוּ Ezek 47:9; Ezek 47:11, וַיֵּרָפו (Gesl.c.) 2Kgs 2:22, etc.; Infinitive construct הֵרָפֵא Jer 15:18 +, הֵרָפֵה (Idib.) Jer 19:11 — be healed:
1. literally, of person 1Sam 6:3 + accusative of disease Deut 28:27; Deut 28:35 subject disease Lev 13:18; Lev 13:37; Lev 14:3; Lev 14:48 of (bad) water 2Kgs 2:22, salt waters (prediction), i.e. be made fresh, Ezek 47:8; Ezek 47:9; Ezek 47:11 of (broken) pottery, i.e. be made whole, Jer 19:11 (in simile).
2. figurative, be healed:
\ \ a. of national hurts, subject city Jer 51:8; Jer 51:9 involving forgiveness and ׳י's blessing, impersonal with ל of people, נִרְפָּאלָֿנוּ Isa 53:5 i.e. healing has come to us.
\ \ b. of personal distress, subject person Jer 17:14, subject the distress Jer 15:18. Pi`el Perfect 1 singular רִפִּאתִי 2Kgs 2:21 2 masculine plural רְפֵּאתֶם Ezek 34:4 1 plural רִפִּאנוּ Jer 51:9 Imperfect 3 masculine singular יְרַפֵּא Exod 21:19; Zech 11:16, וַיְרַפֵּא 1Kgs 18:30 3 masculine plural וַיְרַפְּאוּ Jer 6:14, וַיְרַפּוּ (Ges«GKC:75qq»§ 75qq) Jer 8:11 Infinitive absolute רַפֹּא Exod 21:19 — have healed, heal, usually human subject:
1. literal, רַפּאֹ יְרַפֵּא Exod 21:19 he shall have (him) well healed; with accusative of altar, = repair, 1Kgs 18:30 with ל of water (subject ׳י) 2Kgs 2:21.
2. figurative of healing national defects and hurts, accusative of person, Ezek 34:14; Zech 11:16 work at healing, treat (accusative of hurt) Jer 6:14; Jer 8:11 (both עַלנְֿקַלָּה, see [ קָלַל] Niph`al 2), Jer 51:9. Hithpa`el Infinitive construct of purpose, לְהִתְרַפֵּא, literally, in order to get healed, + מִן of wounds 2Kgs 8:29 = 2Kgs 9:15, so || 2Chr 22:6 (read with ᵐ5 מִן for כִּי, compare Be Kau Benz).
